_readme: Digitizers omatouch has actually been run against.
The plugin was written against exactly one touchscreen. Everything here
generalises in principle -- it reads evdev, which is the same everywhere --
but 'in principle' is how plugins come to not work on hardware their author
never had. A vendor that reports pressure differently, a panel whose axes
are inverted, a digitizer that needs a libinput quirk: none of that shows
up until somebody with that hardware tries it.
`scripts/doctor` reads this and tells you whether your digitizer is known.
An unknown one is not a warning -- it is an invitation. Run the doctor, use
the plugin for a day, and open a pull request adding your entry with
whatever did or did not work.
`quirks` is the useful part over time: the specific thing that had to be
done for that device, so the next person with it does not rediscover it.

schema.vendor: USB/i2c vendor id, lowercase hex, as the reader reports it
schema.name: the evdev name string
schema.machine: the laptop or monitor it was found in
schema.slots: how many simultaneous contacts it reports
schema.quirks: anything that had to be done to make it work

digitizers.name: SYNA7501:00 06CB:16D6
digitizers.quirks: None. Reports 10 contacts over i2c, axes match the panel to within 0.4%, and the accelerometer supports auto-rotate and tablet mode.
